note: Machine fields of the rules. The id, level and statement of each rule come from the guides; this file adds the rest. Edit this file, then run tools/build_rules.py.

B-01.rationale: Readers support different schema editions; a file in an unlisted edition may not open or may lose data.
B-01.fix_hint: Export the file in an IFC schema edition the profile accepts (schema.allowed).

B-02.rationale: Without a declared unit a reader must guess; a wrong guess rescales the whole building.
B-02.fix_hint: Declare an IfcSIUnit LENGTHUNIT METRE in the project's unit assignment and model in metres.

examples.bad: no length unit, or .MILLI. METRE with metre-sized numbers

B-03.rationale: A consumer ingests one source file per placement area; others are ignored.
B-03.fix_hint: Merge everything into one master IFC file; keep per-building files only under ifc/alternates/.

examples.bad: three building files all in ifc/

B-04.rationale: Raw non-ASCII bytes are decoded differently by different tools, so names and text change.
B-04.fix_hint: Re-export with one entity per line and encode non-ASCII characters with the format escapes (for example \X2\00B7\X0\).

examples.bad: an entity broken over two lines, or a raw 0xB7 byte

B-05.rationale: Every reader has memory and time limits; a file over them is refused or truncated.
B-05.fix_hint: Reduce geometry (simpler rails, fewer segments, drop hidden detail) or split the work into several placement areas until the file is within the profile's limits.

B-06.rationale: Many readers drop representations they cannot tessellate, silently, so the element vanishes.
B-06.fix_hint: Rebuild the product from extruded profiles, faceted breps or mapped items; avoid swept disks and boolean-heavy breps.

B-07.rationale: Re-ingesting a revision must reproduce the same result or saved references break.
B-07.fix_hint: Make the exporter deterministic: fixed header time, stable ordering, GlobalIds derived from stable keys.

B-08.rationale: Line-oriented tools, diff tools and simple readers handle one-entity-per-line files; wrapped entities are valid but can be missed.
B-08.fix_hint: Re-export with one entity per line, or reformat the file so each entity stays on a single line.

examples.bad: an entity continued on the next line

B-09.rationale: Very large files load slowly and are hard to review.
B-09.fix_hint: Reduce the file below the profile's budgets.recommendedFileMegabytes.

B-10.rationale: A different up axis or handedness turns or mirrors the building.
B-10.fix_hint: Re-export with Z up, +X forward, +Y left, in metres.

B-11.rationale: A consumer attaches the file with zero offset and rotation.
B-11.fix_hint: Move the geometry into the final placement frame; do not rely on the consumer to shift or turn it.

examples.good: local z = 0 at the finished floor of the lowest level
examples.bad: geometry authored 12 m too low and expected to be lifted

B-12.rationale: A written frame note lets a reviewer verify the frame.
B-12.fix_hint: Add a property set on the IfcProject with FrameNote (text) and LevelOffsetMetres (number).

examples.good: FrameNote: metres; +X forward; +Y left; +Z up; local z = 0 at the finished floor

B-13.rationale: Tools that work level by level drop elements that belong to no level.
B-13.fix_hint: Create an IfcBuildingStorey per level with Name and Elevation and put every element in one (IfcRelContainedInSpatialStructure or IfcRelAggregates).

examples.good: every wall contained in its storey

B-14.rationale: The full hierarchy keeps levels grouped by building.
B-14.fix_hint: Add IfcSite and IfcBuilding and aggregate them under the project.

B-15.rationale: Common practice that keeps a model readable, identifiable and usable by many different consumers.
B-15.fix_hint: Change the work so that it meets the rule statement, then rerun the check named in how_to_check.

B-20.rationale: Tools derive a room's floor, area and position from its solid; without a flat floor they cannot.
B-20.fix_hint: Model each room as an IfcSpace whose solid is an upward extrusion of the floor outline, floor flat at the lowest plane.

examples.good: IfcSpace extruded 3.0 m from the floor outline

B-21.rationale: A room without geometry cannot be located, measured or shown.
B-21.fix_hint: Give the IfcSpace a Body representation (an extruded solid).

B-22.rationale: Duplicate identifiers make every reference to a room ambiguous.
B-22.fix_hint: Add RoomId (IfcPropertySingleValue in an IfcPropertySet linked by IfcRelDefinesByProperties) and make every value unique across the consumer model.

examples.good: RoomId A-101 on one room only

B-23.rationale: Identifiers are printed on labels and stored in fixed-width fields.
B-23.fix_hint: Change the room identifier to meet the profile (identifiers.roomIdMaxLength and identifiers.roomIdPattern).

B-24.rationale: Occupant selects the organisation rules for finishes, lights and counts.
B-24.fix_hint: Set Occupant to one string from the profile's identifiers.occupants, spelled exactly (or to a clear organisation or use when the profile lists none).

B-25.rationale: A consumer's rules read the word Circulation at the start of Function.
B-25.fix_hint: Add Function text; start circulation rooms with the profile's identifiers.circulationPrefix when it names one.

B-26.rationale: Tools that find no identifier invent one from the name, which changes when the name changes.
B-26.fix_hint: Add a RoomId property to the named room.

B-130.rationale: The consumer samples one terrain element; two terrain elements, a mesh that is not a triangulated face set, or an element outside the site cannot be found or trusted, and pads cut into it make the model disagree with the world.
B-130.fix_hint: Write exactly one IfcGeographicElement TERRAIN contained in the IfcSite with one IfcTriangulatedFaceSet body, built by tools/terrain_import.py from the source patch; do not edit it.

examples.good: one TERRAIN element on the site, imported unchanged
examples.bad: a terrain with a building pad cut into it

B-131.rationale: Consumers look up the ground by plan position; an overhang, hole or overlap gives two heights or none for the same point.
B-131.fix_hint: Rebuild the terrain from the source patch with tools/terrain_import.py; every triangle must face up, edges are shared by at most two triangles and the triangles cover the patch rectangle once.

examples.good: a triangulated rectangle, all normals up
examples.bad: a flipped triangle, or a hole in the patch

B-132.rationale: A patch that stops short of the footprint cannot say where the ground is under the building.
B-132.fix_hint: Ask the terrain source for a larger patch (at least the footprint plus the margin) and import again.

examples.good: patch extends 10 m beyond the lowest level

B-133.rationale: Positions in the file and in the world are tied together only by the georeference; without it the terrain heights cannot be related to the floor.
B-133.fix_hint: Add IfcMapConversion (SourceCRS the model context, TargetCRS an IfcProjectedCRS named as the profile's crsName, XAxisAbscissa 1, XAxisOrdinate 0, Scale 1, OrthogonalHeight the floor height above sea level) and keep frame.levelOffsetMetres at 0.

examples.good: IfcProjectedCRS named as the consumer's custom CRS
examples.bad: an EPSG name the consumer does not use, or no georeference

B-134.rationale: A site elevation that disagrees with the terrain gives two answers to how high the ground is.
B-134.fix_hint: Set IfcSite.RefElevation to the terrain height at the building origin above sea level.

examples.good: RefElevation equals the ground height at the origin
examples.bad: RefElevation left at 0 on a hill

B-135.rationale: A building on seabed is under water in the consumer's world.
B-135.fix_hint: Move the building to ground at or above sea level, or ask the terrain source for a different site.

examples.good: all footprint points at or above sea level

B-136.rationale: A building that is above or below the ground everywhere was placed at the wrong height: it hovers or is buried.
B-136.fix_hint: Send the source the correct finished floor elevation so that it grades the pad to it, then import the new patch.

examples.bad: floor 3 m above the ground everywhere

B-136.estimate: terrain heights at sampled points of the footprint

B-137.rationale: Heights near water change between source versions; a delivery that does not say which version it used cannot be reproduced or compared.
B-137.fix_hint: Write every property of Pset_Declaration_Terrain from the sidecar; tools/terrain_import.py does it.

B-138.rationale: Terrain is the largest mesh in a delivery and drives load time.
B-138.fix_hint: Import with a larger error bound or a coarser source level.

examples.good: under the profile's terrain triangle cap
examples.bad: a million triangles of flat ground

B-139.rationale: Sea and shoreline are the terrain source's business; the file only needs to say how the building relates to them.
B-139.fix_hint: Write SeaLevelMetres, FootprintInWater and (when known) DistanceToShoreMetres on the site; do not model water.

examples.bad: a water surface modelled as a slab

B-140.rationale: A number without a stated frame is applied in the wrong frame by someone.
B-140.fix_hint: Set Pset_Declaration_Terrain.Frame to the file frame statement (x east, y north, z up, relative to the lowest finished floor).

examples.good: Frame says x east, y north, z up

X-23.rationale: The terrain source can change between versions; the receiving party must be able to tell exactly which version the heights came from.
X-23.fix_hint: Put terrain/patch.tif and terrain/patch.json in the package and add the manifest terrain section equal to the sidecar.

examples.bad: terrain files present but not pinned

B-141.rationale: On a stepped site several levels meet the ground at different heights; the terrain source can only grade what it is told about.
B-141.fix_hint: Add Pset_Declaration_Level with GroundContact true to every level that touches the ground.

examples.bad: a lower terrace level left undeclared

B-142.rationale: Content below the lowest floor means the origin sits at the wrong height or something is buried by mistake.
B-142.fix_hint: Move the origin to the lowest finished floor, or make the element a slab, footing, pile, wall, stair or ramp (openings, terrain and reservation volumes are exempt).

examples.good: footings and a buried stair below z 0
examples.bad: a door below the lowest floor

B-143.rationale: Consumers that look for enclosed rooms must be able to tell an open-air room from an internal one.
B-143.fix_hint: Give open-air rooms PredefinedType EXTERNAL and Enclosed false; give internal rooms Enclosed true or none.

examples.good: a terrace as EXTERNAL with Enclosed false
examples.bad: a courtyard modelled as an internal room

B-144.rationale: Rain, snow, sight lines and shadows depend on the real pitch and the lean of walls.
B-144.fix_hint: Model the roof as sloped IfcSlab ROOF pieces and a battered wall as one IfcWall with an inclined section.

examples.good: two sloped roof slabs meeting at a ridge
examples.bad: a roof stepped in flat boxes

X-70.rationale: Reviewers and the intake tool find a delivery by its folder and its manifest, and a handle ties it to its author.
X-70.fix_hint: Rename the folder to the slug used as delivery.id, add the missing fields to the submission object of delivery.json (schemas/submission.schema.json) and rerun.

examples.bad: deliveries/My Study/ with no submission object

X-71.rationale: A catalogue entry must carry uniform, known terms for everyone who uses it later.
X-71.fix_hint: Set submission.licence to one of the licences the profile lists (CC-BY-4.0 or CC0-1.0 by default) and make the provenance entries agree.

X-72.rationale: A delivery is data; anything that can run or unpack itself is a risk to every person and tool that opens it.
X-72.fix_hint: Remove the file, or convert the content to a listed type (ifc, glb, png, jpg, json, md, csv, txt); clear the executable bit with chmod -x.

X-73.rationale: Review and intake run on shared machines with fixed time and memory.
X-73.fix_hint: Remove files that are not needed, reduce texture sizes or geometry, or split the delivery into two deliveries.

examples.bad: 900 files or a single 80 MB texture

X-74.rationale: A path that leaves the delivery folder or collides on another system can overwrite or hide a file.
X-74.fix_hint: Rename the file to letters, digits, dot, hyphen and underscore, without a leading dot, and make every path in delivery.json and SHA256SUMS.txt relative with forward slashes.

X-75.rationale: A link can point outside the delivery and make a reader open a file that was never submitted.
X-75.fix_hint: Replace the link by a copy of the file it points to.

X-76.rationale: The maintainers cannot check ownership, so the statement is on record with the delivery.
X-76.fix_hint: Set the three attestation fields to true only if they are true, otherwise do not submit the delivery.

examples.good: ownWork, mayLicense and noRestrictedContent all true

X-77.rationale: A renamed file can hide content from review and can crash a reader.
X-77.fix_hint: Re-export the file in the type its name says, within the pixel limit, or rename it to its real type if that is allowed.

examples.good: a PNG with a PNG header

X-78.rationale: A reviewer sees the work before opening a model.
X-78.fix_hint: Add a rendered or plotted picture to previews/ (tools/preview.py draws plans and an isometric view).

X-79.rationale: One file must say exactly which models and pictures belong to which source, so that a change after the fact is visible.
X-79.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG; it writes proofs/manifest.json and everything it lists. Delete files in proofs/ that it did not write.

examples.good: proofs/manifest.json lists 6 GLB files, a report and 14 renders, each with its hash

X-80.rationale: A GLB that is malformed, in another unit or axis, or that points outside itself shows consumers a different building than the IFC file or crashes them.
X-80.fix_hint: Re-export with python3 tools/export_glb.py (do not edit GLB files by hand), then run python3 tools/validate_glb.py on them and fix what it names; each finding carries a code and a hint.

examples.good: a GLB in metres, Y up, every buffer used, unit normals
examples.bad: a GLB whose image is a file name, or whose triangles exceed limits.maxTriangles

X-81.rationale: The GLB files are what the pictures are made from and what a consumer without an IFC reader opens; they must correspond to the delivered source and be known to be valid.
X-81.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG after the last change to any IFC file, texture set or item; it regenerates the GLB files and the validation report together.

examples.good: one GLB per item, covering, fixture, door, window and texture set, plus model.glb, and a passing report
examples.bad: a new chair added to the IFC file but no GLB for it

X-82.rationale: A picture set that leaves out a level, a kind of room or a component lets a defect there go unseen.
X-82.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG; it renders the standard set. A room needs a Function property so that its kind is known.

examples.good: a plan for every level, four views of each room kind, four exterior views, a sheet per component
examples.bad: a second level with no plan

X-83.rationale: A picture that cannot be traced to the exact model it shows proves nothing about it.
X-83.fix_hint: Re-render with python3 tools/build_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG; do not rename, resize or edit the pictures afterwards.

examples.good: a render whose glb hash is the hash of proofs/glb/model.glb
examples.bad: a render made from an earlier version of the model

X-84.rationale: Pictures are for looking at on shared machines: a very large one costs every reviewer and a tiny one shows nothing.
X-84.fix_hint: Use the default sizes of tools/render.py; lower --scale only within the profile's minimum and raise nothing above its maximum.

X-85.rationale: A file that records who made it, where or on which machine leaks that to everyone who receives the delivery.
X-85.fix_hint: Rebuild the proofs with tools/build_proofs.py, which writes images and GLB files without metadata. For your own pictures, re-save them without EXIF, XMP or text chunks.

examples.good: a PNG with only IHDR, IDAT and IEND chunks
examples.bad: a PNG with a tEXt chunk naming a folder on someone's disk

X-86.rationale: Proofs that cannot be reproduced cannot be trusted, and a rebuild is the cheapest way to see that the pictures show the model.
X-86.fix_hint: Run python3 tools/check_proofs.py deliveries/SLUG --reproduce with the pinned requirements (tools/requirements-ci.txt); if the GLB bytes differ, rebuild the proofs with that toolchain.

examples.good: the rebuilt GLB files are byte-identical and every re-render is within tolerance
examples.bad: a render edited after it was made
